plain: The Orion correlation theory holds that the great pyramids on the Giza Plateau in Egypt are laid out to match the stars of Orion's belt. The writer Graham Hancock credits it to the author Robert Bauval, saying he came up with it in 1994 in his book The Orion Mystery, published that year. The researcher Geoffrey Drumm also brings it up. He says some of these structures "are connected to Orion's belt" and adds "I think that's true," but does not name Bauval or give a date. The theory is told because, if right, it would mean the pyramid builders planned their monuments around the sky.
